title: The Physical Riverbed Hypothesis: Structural Boundaries and Cross-Hardware Validation of an Embodied Evolution System under Extreme Constraints
abstract: The core tenet of embodied intelligence holds that intelligence emerges from the coupling among a body, its environment, and simple control laws, yet the deeper question of to what extent the physical structure itself acts as an algorithm has long lacked an operationally testable formulation. This paper reports an embodied evolution system completed under extreme resource constraints (three months, a single developer, no off-the-shelf platform): an obstacle-escape robot driven by novelty search and deployed on two heterogeneous ESP32 hardware platforms. Under the "no-calibration, no-filtering, no-PID" principles, the system consumes hardware thermal noise as its input and relies on a structure-first data pipeline (magic-number validation, fixed-width delta compression, CRC32 checksums, and atomic writes) to enable remote recomputation of process data. The analysis adopts self-controlled differencing and MAD-robust cleaning, taking the non-triggering of pre-registered falsification conditions as the acceptance criterion. Based on nine baseline datasets spanning 20+ generations and one heterogeneous-hardware dataset spanning 10 generations, three conclusions emerge. First, structural signatures-novelty that rises then plateaus, a non-degenerating rule count, and chaos constrained to left-wheel deceleration-reproduce stably across hardware and firmware versions, supporting the main conjecture. Second, the weak-version hypothesis (that specific sensor parameters directly determine specific behaviors) is rejected as a Simpson pseudo-correlation once environmental confounds are removed; physical structure therefore acts not as a rigid rope that directly drives behavior, but as a physical riverbed that constrains the parameter-evolution space through epistatic effects. Third, when the perceptual information bandwidth is degraded and the noise-source pin is polluted by on-chip Flash multiplexing, the algorithm retains basic diversity, yet capability-side metrics (speed, survival, and the four-class criteria) become non-computable owing to acquisition defects. The paper thereby delineates the applicable boundary of the physical riverbed hypothesis and argues that data provenance is the only bridge capable of turning process-state data into scientific evidence.
